\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{कमावणो} (kamāvṇo)}{कमावणो (kamāvṇo)}]{\mw{कमावणो} (kamāvṇo) — to earn}

\label{lesson:MW-C194-kamavno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for in cash, then the Marwadi for to pay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{कमावणो}}
\textbf{\mw{कमावणो}} — \emph{kamāvṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to earn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{मां} \mw{हाट} \mw{मांय} \mw{पैसा} \mw{कमावै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mā̃ hāṭ mā̃y paisā kamāvai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mother earns money at the weekly market.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{सो} \mw{रुपिया} \mw{कमाया}, \emph{mhaĩ so rupiyā kamāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{कमावणो}} (\emph{kamāvṇo}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*karmāpayati}, \textquotedblleft{}works, earns\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry, but lists Hindi \emph{kamānā}, \textquotedblleft{}earns\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2897).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kamāvṇo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kamāvṇo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mā̃ hāṭ mā̃y paisā kamāvai hai.} — Mother earns money at the weekly market.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for in cash, then the Marwadi for to pay, then say \emph{kamāvṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{कमावणो} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To earn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{खरचणो} (kharchṇo)}{खरचणो (kharchṇo)}]{\mw{खरचणो} (kharchṇo) — to spend}

\label{lesson:MW-C194-kharchno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to pay, then the Marwadi for to earn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{खरचणो}}
\textbf{\mw{खरचणो}} — \emph{kharchṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to spend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{हूं} \mw{बाजार} \mw{मांय} \mw{घणा} \mw{पैसा} \mw{खरचूं} \mw{हूं।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hū̃ bājār mā̃y ghaṇā paisā kharchū̃ hū̃.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I spend a lot of money at the market.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{दस} \mw{रुपिया} \mw{खरच्या}, \emph{mhaĩ das rupiyā kharchyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{खरचणो}} (\emph{kharchṇo}) is a verb made on \emph{kharch}, \textquotedblleft{}expense\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{kharj}, \textquotedblleft{}expenditure\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{उधार} (udhār)}{उधार (udhār)}]{\mw{उधार} (udhār) — credit; a loan}

\label{lesson:MW-C194-udhar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a salary, then the Marwadi for a profit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{उधार}}
\textbf{\mw{उधार}} — \emph{udhār} — \textquotedblleft{}credit; a loan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{अठै} \mw{उधार} \mw{कोनी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aṭhai udhār konī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
No credit here.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{उधार}} (\emph{udhār}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{uddhāra}, \textquotedblleft{}raising; a loan\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry, but lists Hindi \emph{udhār}, \textquotedblleft{}debt\textquotedblright{}, and Gujarati \emph{udhāro}, \textquotedblleft{}credit account\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2018).
\end{cousinweb}
